## The forcing loop: parsing, registration and the stage increment (`forcing:`) {#sec-ch09-framework}

### Summary

snapy treats every source term other than the flux divergence as a *forcing*: a module that reads the
stage-entry primitives and the temperature and adds its contribution, multiplied by the full step $\Delta t$, to
the increment the flux divergence started. The modules run in a fixed order, they all read the same primitives and
temperature, and none of them reads the others' contributions, so the order does not change the result. The loop
also records how much dry-air density the modules added, so that passive tracers can be carried with it.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Turns each key of the YAML block `forcing:` into one module that adds $\Delta t\,\mathbf S$, with $\mathbf S$ the module's source per unit volume
[conserved units per $\mathrm{s}$], to the stage increment $\Delta\mathbf U$; @eq-ch09-framework-stage.

**Data.** In: the stage primitives $\mathbf W$ and the temperature $T$ [$\mathrm{K}$] = `W->T` of the same $\mathbf W$, cell
averages on the block including ghosts, and $\Delta t$ [$\mathrm{s}$]. Out: the conserved stage increment $\Delta\mathbf U$
(per unit volume, total-mass basis, interior and ghost cells) and, when the block carries passive scalars, the
modules' dry-density increment `_forcing_dry` [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$]. Check case: three toy modules on a 12-cell
row with one ghost each side.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, in `HydroImpl::forward`, after the flux divergence and before the gravity-work
bookkeeping and the vertical implicit correction; modules in a fixed registration order.

**Activation.** The presence of each key; no key, no module. Default: no forcing.

**Guarantee / limits.** The sum does not depend on the module order, up to round-off; each module is first order in
time within a stage.

**Evidence.** Tests: the parser refuses `fric-heat` and unknown keys,
{{< code tests/test_hydro_options.cpp hydro_options.reject_removed_and_unknown_forcing_keys >}} (exact); a MeshBlock
with `body-heat` and the three relaxations constructs,
{{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.meshblock_registers_parent_dependent_modules >}}; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` are
linear in $\Delta t$, {{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.boundary_fluxes_scale_with_timestep >}} (`allclose`
defaults); these ctests were not run at the pin. Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/framework_check.py`, output `framework_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C3]`, re-run at the pin: all PASS, output identical (Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0).
:::

The YAML parser refuses unknown keys under `forcing:`, and refuses the key `fric-heat` with a message that
explains why: the $x_1$ face gravity work already carries the sedimentation part of the mass flux, so that term
would release the precipitation potential energy twice. Twelve keys are accepted: `const-gravity` (@sec-ch06),
`coriolis`, `diffusion`, `body-heat`, `top-cool`, `bot-heat`, `relax-bot-comp`, `relax-bot-temp`,
`relax-bot-velo`, `top-sponge-lyr`, `bot-sponge-lyr` and `plume-forcing`. The last is accepted but never installed
(@sec-ch09-plume).

### Derivation

Let $\mathbf U$ be the conserved variables per unit volume, $\mathbf F$ the numerical flux vector through the cell
faces (NOTATION.md $\mathbf F_a$), and $\mathbf S^m$ the source per unit volume of module $m = 1..M$. The continuous
balance, its integral over cell $i$ divided by $V_i$, and the semi-discrete form are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\mathbf U + \nabla\cdot\mathbf F &= \sum_{m=1}^{M}\mathbf S^m, \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}\overline{\mathbf U}_i}{\mathrm{d}t}
 &= -\frac{1}{V_i}\sum_{f\in\partial i}A_f\,\mathbf F_f\cdot\mathbf n_f + \sum_{m=1}^{M}\overline{\mathbf S}^m_i, \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}\overline{\mathbf U}_i}{\mathrm{d}t} &= \mathcal L_i(\mathbf U)
 \equiv -(\nabla\cdot\mathbf F)_i + \sum_{m=1}^{M}\mathbf S^m_i(\mathbf W, T),
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second line uses the divergence theorem with $A_f$ and $\mathbf n_f$ the area and outward normal of face $f$,
and the third writes the face sum as the discrete divergence $(\nabla\cdot\mathbf F)_i$ of @sec-ch03. The
third line is also where the scheme truncates: each module evaluates its source on the cell values $\mathbf W_i$ and
$T_i$, not as the cell average of the pointwise source, which is exact for a source linear in the state and
second-order accurate otherwise. One stage forms the increment

$$
\Delta\mathbf U_i = -\Delta t\,(\nabla\cdot\mathbf F)_i + \Delta t\sum_{m=1}^{M}\mathbf S^{m}_i(\mathbf W, T)
$$ {#eq-ch09-framework-stage}

and hands it to the integrator, which forms $\mathbf U \leftarrow w_0^{(s)}\mathbf U^n + w_1^{(s)}\mathbf U + w_2^{(s)}\Delta\mathbf U$,
where $w_0^{(s)}, w_1^{(s)}, w_2^{(s)}$ are the dimensionless weights of RK stage $s$ (@sec-ch07-rk).
@eq-ch09-framework-stage is built in `HydroImpl::forward`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}): the divergence term on interior cells, then the
module loop. Each $\mathbf S^m$ is evaluated on the same $\mathbf W$ and on $T$ computed once from it with
`W->T`, so the sum does not depend on the order of the loop; only round-off does. Beyond the three lines above, the loop is a sum. A port of the assembly with three toy modules that read only $\mathbf W$ and $T$
checks its properties: the six loop orders give the same increment to $4.4\times10^{-16}$ of its size, and the
increment is linear in $\Delta t$.[^fw-c1] The tests below check linearity and registration on the real modules.

The dry-air part of the modules' increment, $\Delta\rho_{\mathrm{d}}^{\mathrm{forc}} = \Delta\mathbf U[\rho_{\mathrm{d}}]$
after the loop minus before it, is stored as `_forcing_dry`, and only when the block carries passive scalars and
has at least one module ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). It holds the modules' dry
increment only, not the divergence term, and is not formed without tracers.[^fw-c3] The tracer carry that
consumes it is @sec-ch10-tracer.

[^fw-c1]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/framework_check.py`, output `framework_check.out`, lines `[C1]` and `[C2]`;
    a numpy port of the assembly in `HydroImpl::forward` at the pin, three toy modules, double precision.
[^fw-c3]: Same command, line `[C3]`: maximum error $2.8\times10^{-17}$ with tracers; without tracers the stored
    increment is undefined.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-framework-order shows the registration order and where the increment goes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-framework-order
#| fig-cap: "Registration order of the native forcing modules. Each sky-blue box is a module, numbered in the order it is installed; the dashed box is accepted by the parser but never installed. The orange line is the flux-divergence increment $\\Delta\\mathbf U=-\\Delta t\\,\\nabla\\cdot\\mathbf F$ the loop starts from, and the green line what happens to the increment after the loop."
#| fig-alt: "Twelve boxes in three rows of four, numbered 1 to 12 and connected by arrows, with plume-forcing dashed; a text line above for the start of the increment and one below for what follows it."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_framework_order import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The loop runs in every Runge–Kutta stage, inside `HydroImpl::forward`, after the flux divergence and before the
gravity-work bookkeeping and the vertical implicit correction (@sec-ch06 and @sec-ch07). All modules are explicit.
Each module decides which cells it touches: `body-heat` touches interior cells only, the diffusion module adds a
divergence of face fluxes, and the boundary modules (`top-cool`, `bot-heat`, the three relaxations, the two
sponges) act only on a block that owns the physical $x_1$ boundary they name. Increments a module writes into
ghost cells do not survive: the ghosts are refilled after the stage (@sec-ch11).

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| refuse `fric-heat` | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `fric-heat` | refused key |

| per-module parsing | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `from_yaml` | each key |
| install in fixed order | {{< code src/hydro/register_forcing_modules.cpp HydroImpl::_register_forcings_module >}} | `_register_forcings_module` | each key |

: Code map of the forcing loop. {#tbl-ch09-framework-code}

1. `HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml` refuses `fric-heat`, checks the keys with `check_keys` and parses each module's
   options with its own `from_yaml` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The
   `plume-forcing` options are parsed only when the equation of state is `plume-eos`.
2. `HydroImpl::reset` calls `_register_forcings_module`, which appends the modules in the order of
   @fig-ch09-framework-order ({{< code src/hydro/register_forcing_modules.cpp HydroImpl::_register_forcings_module >}}),
   and registers each as a submodule under its key ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
3. Each stage, `HydroImpl::forward` starts the increment from the divergence on interior cells, computes $T$ once
   and runs the loop ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
4. `MeshBlockImpl::advance_local` hands the dry increment to the tracers with `carry_dry_source`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}).

### Limits

1. **Ghost-cell increments.** Modules that do not restrict themselves to interior cells (the sponges, and
   `top-cool` and `bot-heat` across $x_2$, $x_3$) also write into ghost cells. The refill after the stage
   overwrites them. Not a defect; stated so that a reader of `du` is not surprised.
2. **Immersed solids.** The loop sees the solid placeholder state that `mark_prim_solid_` writes into $\mathbf W$
   before it ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). The diffusion module is the worked case
   (@sec-ch09-wallcoef); the relaxations and `body-heat` read the same state and are not measured.
3. **`plume-forcing`** is accepted by the parser and never installed (@sec-ch09-plume).
4. **Untested combinations.** No ctest steps two boundary modules together through the solver. See the switch
   coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
